svg.title: on the common field domain. To check the identity operator in this formula, first insert a unit label in any Euclidean correlation and use the hierarchy’s unit law to remove it. The two corresponding strict complex-time functions agree on imaginary times and hence everywhere by holomorphic uniqueness. Smearing in that slot gives R f times the remaining function, by Fubini, and passing to the tempered boundary gives the same Wightman identity. Pair the resulting word vectors with arbitrary word vectors. Their dense span implies that unit insertion is ( R f)I on the common domain. Linearity then proves (TR1). Similarly the Euclidean one-point function of Θ is zero; holomorphic uniqueness and the boundary limit prove its vanishing vacuum matrix element. Reality and scalar covariance follow from the stress tensor and the real invariant unit. Let E(s) = ⟨Θ(−s 2e0)Θ( s 2e0)⟩E, s > 0.
